summary:
I rendered the 2D->3D proof of concept "The cloth becomes the board" for f1664-1782: 119 frames at native 2560x1440 and 30 fps, muxed with the matching audio slice (samples 2446080..2621010). The mp4 is H.264 High, yuv420p, tagged bt709 and tv range, CRF 14, with 192k AAC audio. I checked it by decoding frames from the encoded file. There is no upscale: Eevee rendered at 1440p with 16 TAA.

**Board layout (seed 4242).**
- I captured UI-free demo-mode plates from the live game (zoom 11 and zoom 30, units hidden). I back-projected them through the decoded camera rig onto the hex grid. Sablon, Grandbois, Hautecouronne and the sea's position all align with the menu's first frame (see compare_f1782_vs_menu.jpg).
- Vaugrise and Brumecourt sit under the menu card, so I took them from the demo world.
- The layout is in data/layout.json and data/pieces.json.

**f1664-1719: the 2D stitch-on (R25 code, unchanged, 6 px/mm, about 84k recorded stitches).**
- The board is padded satin hex coupons in greens, wheat, ochre and terracotta, a laid-and-couched denim sea with stem-stitched wave marks, and a pale-blue running-stitch sea grid.
- Hex seams are cream running stitch, the coast has a brown stem outline, and realm borders are couched gold pairs with tie-downs in the realm colour. Also stitched: a river cord, crop plots, hill mounds and peaks, elevation icons re-embroidered from the game's own models, and the game's figure cards as appliqué slips.
- A wavefront spreads from Grandbois on twos. In each hex the padding goes down first, then each strand grows along its length. Iron-gall underdrawing shows on bare linen ahead of the wave. The last hex closes on f1719.

**f1720-1725: the swap.** It is a linear-light dissolve to the Eevee zero-tilt still. The Eevee ground's emission is the R25 radiance texture of the same final state, so the two match by construction. Measured: median ΔE_ok×100 of 0.66 per pixel (0.14 after a 2 px low-pass) and a 0.08 px global shift.

**f1726-1766: the crane (Blender 4.0.2 legacy Eevee).** The camera goes from pitch 90 to the decoded menu camera (vfov 30, pitch 66.087, distance 20.9, target Grandbois + (-2.2, 0, 0.5)). It is 0.008° off the menu pitch at f1760 and exact at f1766.
- The baked relief grows in, and the coupons swell as padded cushions on twos.
- 89 pieces rise between f1728 and f1748, all settled by f1760: 5 towns from the game OBJs (with banner), 2 quarries, lumber camps, pines and 21 figure cards. They use a stitch material port (game palette, laid-wool bump, brown inverted-hull outline).
- Each piece pops up on twos, hinging off its stitched elevation icon. On the frame it starts, its footprint appears behind it: padding felt with underdrawing and needle holes, visible for at least 34 frames. 410 wool tethers stretch, snap one by one between 6 and 10 frames into each rise, and their ends curl.
- Shadows and contact shadows come from Eevee and reach the R25 ground through a Shader-to-RGB lighting ratio. Towns press the padding flat under themselves. Camera motion blur (180° shutter) is added in COMP using ground-plane homographies.

**f1767-1782:** the camera holds on the menu pose, with a +0.25 EV light swell peaking at f1760, then settling.

**Visual iterations, each inspected as stills, 1:1 crops, contact sheets and decoded mp4 frames.**
1. R25 look-dev: colours, and a padding underlay so strand gaps read as grooves rather than pale linen.
2. Full bake: removed a crease bug that erased part of the sea; softened the couching bars; made the gold borders bolder.
3. First Eevee: moved the key to the left-front because pieces were back-lit; fixed half-buried pines; changed footprints from white linen to felt; resized towns and figure cards; shortened the tethers.
4. Colour match against the menu: deep denim sea and lower exposure; fixed stray fibres appearing on bare linen.
5. Full 720p preview: switched to COMP motion blur because Eevee's own blur had no effect; towns sink less now that the padding is pressed flat under them; stronger underdrawing ahead of the wave.

All animation is a function of the frame number and reproducible from the scripts. src/README.md-level instructions are in README.md, alongside qa.json, a contact sheet, the A/B swap image with a difference image, and the comparison with the menu.
render_cost:
Measured on the 4-core machine shared with other agents.
- Eevee legacy, 2560x1440, 16 TAA: 48-100 s per frame, about 60 s on average. 42 frames are in the film (f1725 still plus f1726-1766; the hold f1767-1782 reuses f1766). I rendered 54 frames at 1440p in total: the 42 kept, 11 discarded after the padding-press fix, and 1 look-dev frame. That is inside the roughly 60-frame budget.
- The 720p preview passes (8 TAA, 42 frames each) took 11-17 s per frame.
- R25 board bake: about 100 s. Wavefront replay, final and ghost states, fibres and full-board radiance: about 100 s.
- R25 2D frames: 28 unique states at about 6-8 s each on 2 numba threads, about 4 minutes in total.
- COMP: about 1.5 s per frame at 1440p, including the 9-sample homography motion blur.
- x264 encode: under 1 minute, 19 MB.
- Wall time of the last full final pass (Eevee, COMP, encode, QA): about 45 minutes.
self_critique:
**What works.**
- The 2D phase is the strongest part. At 1:1 it reads as real embroidery: padded satin coupons with strand direction, padding felt under the growing strands, couched gold borders with tie-downs, a laid-and-couched denim sea with wave marks, seams, and underdrawing on bare linen ahead of a believable wavefront.
- The swap is invisible by construction. It measures ΔE_ok×100 of 0.66 and a 0.08 px shift.
- The crane lands exactly on the decoded menu camera, and the final frame registers with the live menu's layout.
- The pop-up hinges, footprints, tethers and Eevee shadows read clearly in 1:1 crops.

**Weaknesses compared with an AAA bar.**
- The 3D pieces are the game's low-poly OBJs with only a bump-level stitch port, so they read as painted toys more than embroidery. The pines in particular look like pale fabric cones on their lit side.
- The final board is sparser and lighter than the menu's: fewer pines, smaller crop plots, lighter satin, and no unit shield markers or nameplates.
- The satin's anisotropic sheen is baked for the face-on view. During the 24° crane only the diffuse response changes, so the satin does not flash as it would physically.
- The stitch-on uses a sweep within each hex. Up close the growing front can look like confetti rather than a single needle path.
- Tethers are thin and short. They are readable at 1:1 but subtle at full frame.
- I could not afford another full 1440p pass to push forest density and darker satin without breaking the Eevee budget.
known_issues: Town, tree and figure icons are stitched as Bayeux-style elevations (lying flat, top toward the far side) rather than plan icons. This is what makes the pop-up hinge possible and keeps the footprint visible behind each risen piece; a plan icon would be hidden under its own model. It departs from the brief's wording 'plan-icon towns'.

Vaugrise, Brumecourt and the extent of the red realm come from the demo-mode world (4 players, played to turn 16). They sit under the menu card, so the menu cannot confirm them, and their development state may differ from the menu world.
There are no game shield markers above unit groups and no in-world nameplates. Forests are less dense, and the board is lighter and less saturated than the live menu (see compare_f1782_vs_menu.jpg).
Eevee legacy's own motion blur had no effect on the python-driven frames. Camera motion blur is applied in COMP through ground-plane homographies and is approximate for tall pieces.
The ground's specular and sheen are baked for the face-on view in the R25 radiance texture. Under the crane only Eevee's diffuse lighting ratio (swell, shadows, AO) responds.

Frames f1725-1727 come from the first final run and f1728-1766 from the second, after the padding-press and pine-colour fixes. The first three frames show no pieces and a flat ground, so they are unaffected.
Desk chrome, valance, leaf and aspect buckets are out of scope, as the director directed. The f1760 keyframe therefore shows the board only.
The 720p preview mp4 in preview/ predates the last fixes: motion blur, underdrawing boost and the padding press.
